correctness.rationale: With one-dimensional complement, the exact left-preconditioned error matrix orthogonally reduces in singular values to T_alpha=[[0,-c],[-alpha p,1-alpha d]]. A determinant PSD criterion yields W_z F_z(alpha_z)=z(z-c^2)[(d^2+p^2)z-p^2(1+c^2)], proving a global squared-norm lower bound max(c^2,p^2(1+c^2)/(d^2+p^2)). Each branch supplies a positive scalar attaining it, with unique equality; b=0 and branch equality are treated. Strict Euclidean contraction holds precisely for c<1 and d>pc. Similarity to an SPD symmetrically preconditioned matrix and a Schur complement prove the exact spectral stability interval alpha<2/(d+tau). The explicit SPD witness has exact Schur complement 1/10, alpha_opt=810/2429, minimum squared norm=2550/2429>1, and spectral interval (0,10/13). A separately executed symbolic identity check and the extracted Python test routine (one exact witness, 3,500 random SPD blocks and four alternative alpha values each) reproduced all relevant finite instances; tests are not universal proofs.

originality.rationale: The September 2026 originating preprint fixes the precise Type-II inverse action and proves nonsingularity but uses Type I for its Richardson estimate and does not optimize Euclidean one-step error. Older full-text Schur-complement/block-preconditioner literature covers eigenvalues and Krylov iteration counts, not the scalar Euclidean minimax. The closest published weighted-Jacobi result varies a global step for a fixed inverse, whereas this theorem varies only the complement block; no statement-to-statement implication establishes the piecewise optimizer. Detailed searches of aliases, formulas, published findings, and a 3x3 boundary found no covering result. This is a qualified self-review, not certified priority.
residual_risks: Older specialized literature on norm-optimal block Jacobi or approximate inverses may express the same two-by-two scalar singular-value minimax under different notation.
Demmel 2023 journal body was not inspected; its accessible abstract concerns a different condition-number objective, making direct coverage less plausible but not conclusively excluded.
Search and public-record retrieval cannot establish unique worldwide priority or inspect inaccessible/unindexed results.

value.rationale: Type-II ARB adds a scalar inverse action in the orthogonal complement to make a singular reduced-basis approximate inverse usable. Picking that scalar is a natural numerical-analysis decision. This result supplies its exact one-step Euclidean optimum at the first nontrivial complement dimension, a sharp test for whether any scalar guarantees strict one-step error descent, and an open three-dimensional SPD obstruction where the stationary iteration is nevertheless spectrally convergent. The obstruction is sensitive to noncollinearity of b and H^-1 b and cannot arise in two-dimensional SPD blocks with c<1; it is not a table recomputation, renaming, or merely code-backed example. It does not claim multi-step or FGMRES performance.
